description: LeetCode Patterns course graph. Backbone = the 27 practicable patterns of dipjul/Grokking-the-Coding-Interview-Patterns-for-Coding-Questions (`grokking` = its section number). `grokking: null` rows are foundations or extensions the core bank (NeetCode 250 + Striver A2Z) needs that Grokking does not bucket (its only DP pattern is 0/1 knapsack). Omitted: Grokking 27 Multi-thread (its problems are tree traversals; the app runs single-threaded Python) and 28 Miscellaneous. `prereqs` gate unlock order; `encompassing` {prereq: weight} is the share of practice on this node that also exercises that prerequisite (FIRe implicit credit), always a subset of `prereqs`. `describe` is the technique as TypeSafe sees it when tagging problems.

kcs.title: Arrays and strings: traversal and simulation
kcs.describe: Direct iteration over an array or string with index arithmetic, counters or in-place updates; no named algorithmic pattern beyond a loop.

kcs.title: Hash maps: lookup and counting
kcs.describe: A dict or set gives O(1) membership, frequency counts or complement lookups (e.g. two-sum via seen-map, anagram counts).

kcs.title: Prefix sums
kcs.describe: Running cumulative sums (or a map of prefix sums seen) answer range-sum or subarray-sum-equals-k questions in O(1) each.

kcs.title: Two pointers
kcs.describe: Two indices move toward each other or in the same direction over a (usually sorted) array or string: pair sums, dedupe in place, 3Sum, partitioning.

kcs.title: Sliding window
kcs.describe: A contiguous window [left, right] grows and shrinks while maintaining a sum or character counts: longest/shortest substring or subarray under a constraint.

kcs.title: Linked lists: traversal and pointer updates
kcs.describe: Walking ListNode.next, dummy heads, inserting or deleting nodes, merging two sorted lists.

kcs.title: Fast and slow pointers
kcs.describe: Two pointers moving at different speeds detect a cycle, find its start, or find the middle (Floyd's tortoise and hare), on lists or number sequences.

kcs.title: In-place reversal of a linked list
kcs.describe: Reversing a whole linked list, a sub-list, or every k-group by re-pointing next pointers without extra memory.

kcs.title: Cyclic sort
kcs.describe: Numbers in range 1..n are swapped to their own index, then a scan finds missing or duplicate numbers in O(n) time and O(1) space.

kcs.title: Stacks
kcs.describe: A last-in-first-out stack matches brackets, evaluates expressions, simplifies paths or simulates nested structure.

kcs.title: Monotonic stack
kcs.describe: A stack kept increasing or decreasing answers next-greater/next-smaller element, daily temperatures, histogram areas or remove-k-digits.

kcs.title: Recursion
kcs.describe: A function calls itself on a smaller input with a base case: power, reversing via recursion, generating sequences.

kcs.title: Sorting algorithms: merge sort and quick sort
kcs.describe: Implementing or adapting a sort (merge sort, quick sort, counting inversions during merge, custom comparators).

kcs.title: Merge intervals
kcs.describe: Intervals sorted by start are merged, inserted, intersected or counted for overlaps (meeting rooms, free time).

kcs.title: Modified binary search
kcs.describe: Halving a sorted range or a monotone answer space: search in rotated arrays, first/last position, minimum capacity or speed (binary search on the answer).

kcs.title: Bitwise XOR and bit manipulation
kcs.describe: XOR cancellation, masks, shifts and bit counts: single number, complement, counting set bits, subsets as bitmasks.

kcs.title: Math and number theory
kcs.describe: Digit manipulation, primes and sieves, gcd, modular arithmetic or a closed-form formula is the core of the solution.

kcs.title: Binary trees: structure and traversal
kcs.describe: TreeNode basics: preorder/inorder/postorder traversal, height, counting nodes, building or comparing trees.

kcs.title: Tree breadth-first search
kcs.describe: A queue processes a tree level by level: level order, zigzag, level averages, right side view, connecting level siblings.

kcs.title: Tree depth-first search
kcs.describe: Recursive DFS carries state down root-to-leaf paths or combines results up the tree: path sums, diameter, max path sum, lowest common ancestor.

kcs.title: Binary search trees
kcs.describe: The BST ordering invariant drives search, insert, delete, validation, kth smallest or inorder successor.

kcs.title: Graph traversal: BFS and DFS
kcs.describe: BFS or DFS over an adjacency list with a visited set: path exists, connected components, provinces, cloning a graph, bipartite checks.

kcs.title: Island (matrix traversal)
kcs.describe: BFS/DFS over a 2-D grid's 4-neighbours: number of islands, flood fill, closed islands, rotting oranges, surrounded regions.

kcs.title: Topological sort
kcs.describe: Kahn's in-degree queue or DFS post-order orders a DAG: course schedule, task ordering, alien dictionary, cycle detection in directed graphs.

kcs.title: Union find
kcs.describe: Disjoint-set union with path compression merges components: redundant connection, number of provinces, accounts merge.

kcs.title: Heaps and top-K elements
kcs.describe: A heap (heapq) of size k keeps the k largest, smallest, closest or most frequent items; kth largest; task scheduling by frequency.

kcs.title: Two heaps
kcs.describe: A max-heap and a min-heap balance the lower and upper halves: running median, sliding window median, IPO capital.

kcs.title: K-way merge
kcs.describe: A min-heap holds the head of each of k sorted lists or rows: merge k lists, kth smallest in sorted matrix, smallest range.

kcs.title: Shortest paths: Dijkstra and Bellman-Ford
kcs.describe: Weighted shortest paths with a priority queue (Dijkstra), edge relaxation (Bellman-Ford) or Floyd-Warshall: network delay, cheapest flights, path with minimum effort.

kcs.title: Minimum spanning trees
kcs.describe: Kruskal (sorted edges + union find) or Prim (heap) connects all nodes at minimum total weight: min cost to connect points.

kcs.title: Subsets and permutations
kcs.describe: Building every subset, permutation or case variant breadth-first or by include/exclude recursion, handling duplicates.

kcs.title: Backtracking
kcs.describe: Choose, recurse, un-choose with pruning: combination sum, word search, N-queens, sudoku, palindrome partitioning.

kcs.title: Trie
kcs.describe: A prefix tree of child dicts supports insert, prefix search, wildcard search and word-break style lookups.

kcs.title: Greedy algorithms
kcs.describe: A locally optimal choice (often after sorting) is provably globally optimal: jump game, gas station, interval scheduling, assign cookies.

kcs.title: Dynamic programming: 1-D
kcs.describe: A 1-D recurrence over positions, memoised or tabulated: climbing stairs, house robber, decode ways, coin change, word break.

kcs.title: 0/1 knapsack
kcs.describe: Each item is taken or skipped against a capacity or target sum: partition equal subset sum, target sum, count of subset sums.

kcs.title: Dynamic programming: 2-D grids
kcs.describe: A 2-D table over grid cells: unique paths, minimum path sum, maximal square, triangle, cherry pickup.

kcs.title: Dynamic programming on two strings
kcs.describe: A table indexed by prefixes of two sequences: longest common subsequence, edit distance, distinct subsequences, wildcard/regex matching.

kcs.title: Longest increasing subsequence
kcs.describe: LIS-style recurrences, O(n log n) patience sorting with bisect, Russian doll envelopes, largest divisible subset.

kcs.title: Interval and partition DP
kcs.describe: dp[i][j] over a subarray range with a split point: matrix chain multiplication, burst balloons, palindrome partitioning II, minimum cost to cut a stick.

kcs.title: Ordered sets
kcs.describe: A sorted container (bisect over a sorted list) answers floor/ceiling or range queries while items are inserted: my calendar, 132 pattern, longest subarray within a limit.
